exposure: Health insurance coverage (complementary universal health insurance)
Maternal comorbidities (mental illness, cancer, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, hypertension)
Prenatal care utilization (outpatient visits, pelvic ultrasound, blood glucose assay, oral glucose tolerance test)
Hospitalizations during pregnancy (ICU admission, hospital stay, diagnoses for hospital stays)
cohort: The study included 672,182 women covered by the national health insurance general scheme or a local mutualist section, who delivered in France in 2015.
finding: The study comprehensively described the healthcare consumption patterns and maternal health outcomes, including specific rates of comorbidities, prenatal care utilization, hospitalizations, preterm delivery (6.7%), and modes of birth, for over 672,000 women who delivered in France in 2015.
mod_finding: 20% of deliveries were performed by caesarean section, and 16% of vaginal deliveries required instrumental extraction.
cross-section timing: Data on healthcare consumption and delivery outcomes were collected for women who delivered during 2015.
gest_age: Preterm delivery rate (6.7%) was an outcome, implying gestational age was assessed for this metric.
